doc.title: Gerald Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His son Anthony, grandson and Shuggie Otis
summary: Wilson explains his grandson, Shuggie Otis's son by his daughter Terry, writes out his music, and his son Anthony tours with Diana Krall.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: That’s my son, he can write too, by the way. He can write like mad. Just left, he just leaving town for Australia, him and, what’s her name?
Diana Krall, yeah. But my grandson, grandson’s father is one of the greatest blues guitarists around. That’s Shuggie Otis. See, Shuggie Otis is my…
Is he your step son? How does…
‘Cause I thought that was, I thought Shuggie was Johnny Otis’s son.
No, Shuggie is Johnny Otis’s son, yeah, yeah.
Yeah, but see Johnny’s son married my daughter. He married my daughter, see.
Her name is Terry, I named her after Clark Terry

You know, well that’s a middle name, you know, we named her Terry. She know Clark and them, they all used to come, Dizzy. They come, when Dizzy come to town, he would think to come, he would come to my house playing with my daughters, Terry the same way. These all my good buddies, but like I said, now all I do now is. Now, he can play the guitar, you know, Shuggie’s son, he play the guitar. He can write himself, in fact, he’s writing his first orchestration now for a jazz orchestra. But all I do, man, is boom, first trumpet, quarter note tied to an eighth, boom-boom-boom. Dot, eighth rest, so and so and so, I tell him everything he puts on that paper.
